nina: Heads-up: we're scheduling a base image rotation tonight 01:00 UTC. Main concerns: RBAC delta for signer SA, KMS key versioning, offline/HSM clusters, and audit tractability. Want to preflight potential fallout.
mike: Thanks. Can you enumerate exact RBAC changes? Which roles get removed/added?
nina: Plan: grant new signer-sa roles/kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on new key, keep old key enabled, then remove legacy role binding after 6h. Also update IAM policy for image-batcher SA to include signBlob for the new signer flow.
olga: Important: removing a role while nodes still use the old token will cause verifying failures if we flip verification policy too early. Recommend: 1) publish new key, 2) update verifier policy to accept both keys, 3) wait 30m, 4) rotate bindings.
cory: On-prem nuance: our HSM-backed signing appliances don't accept KMS URIs. We need pre-wrapped cosign keys for those clusters. Do we have exportable wrapped keys?
mike: We do NOT have automatically wrapped artifacts for all on-prem clusters. Short-term approach: keep images signed with OLD key in the on-prem registry and delay key rotation for those clusters. Long-term: schedule a HSM integration sprint.
remy: Vulnerability note: the new base includes glibc patch CVE-2026-0007 which changes package set -> artifact digests change. That will break attestation lineage if we don't re-attest artifacts.
nina: So workflow: build patched base -> sign candidate images with NEW key -> push to staging -> run verification canary -> promote. During canary verifier config must accept both signers.
olga: Implementation detail: runtime verification reads trusted keys from `redwood-verifiers` ConfigMap. We can add an array with both fingerprints. Example: ```trusted_keys: ["cosign:sha256:OLD_FINGERPRINT", "cosign:sha256:NEW_FINGERPRINT"]```
mike: Reminder: runtime has an internal verification cache keyed by image digest. If we change trusted keys but don't invalidate cache, some nodes keep rejecting. Command to clear cache: `kubectl -n redwood exec -it runtime-proxy-0 -- /usr/local/bin/cachectl flush` or easier `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/runtime-proxy`.
remy: Audit logging: compliance needs a continuous record showing both signatures for each promoted image. If we re-sign images we must preserve prior signatures and include attestations linking old->new. Otherwise SOC will flag provenance gaps.
nina: Agree. We'll attach both cosign attestations and also export GKE audit logs for the rotation window to gs://redwood-compliance/audit-rotations/YYYYMMDD.
cory: Could SIEM spike on new key usage? We should open a temporary suppression rule matching key_id IN (OLD,NEW) for +48h. I'll file ticket SEC-ROTATE-789.
mike: ops note: don't change signer SA permissions and rotate key in same minute. That race killed pulls during last quarterly rotation. Need staged perms: add new perms first, then flip signer to use new key.
olga: Fallback/rollback playbook (short): 1) revert verification config to ONLY trust OLD key 2) restart runtime proxy 3) re-enable OLD KMS key if disabled 4) pull old image set from `onprem-retain` registry 5) notify oncall. Keep runbook at /confluence/security/base-image-rotations.
remy: Deploy bot: pipeline started: `deploy-bot: base-rotation-ci #884 started (artifact build + cosign attest)`
nina: Action items: mike to create HSM wrapped-key checklist by 14:00 UTC; cory to open SIEM suppression; remy to tag CI with `rotation-window=5401234567`; olga to prepare verifier ConfigMap delta.
mike: Quick command to see cosign key fingerprint: ```cosign public-key <keyfile.pem> | sha256sum``` or for KMS: ```cosign attest --key kms://... --keyid````
nina: I'll post a concise 10-step preflight in 30m and ping oncall. If anything unexpected we abort. :white_check_mark:
